correctness.finding: PASS. Reconstructing the source's numerical geometry with g=10/7, h=8/5 and the stated helicities reproduces all three intended affine triads. The cross-triplet pair P and Q_g generates K_ext=-(P+Q_g)=1.556836734693878+1.372668410498753i with |K_ext|=2.075562377687905, which is separated from the signed seven-mode support by about 0.64807407. The signed retained pair generating this output is unique. Substitution into the source's helical interaction coefficient gives nonzero forcing in both output helicities: approximately -0.01011181242 and -0.00135287564 at t=0. Therefore the seven-mode support is not invariant under the Euler quadratic nonlinearity. This agrees independently with Kishimoto–Yoneda's classification excluding genuinely time-dependent real-valued three-dimensional Euler solutions of finite Fourier support.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Fourier leakage from a non-invariant Galerkin support is standard, and the general finite-mode Euler classification of Kishimoto–Yoneda is prior art. The submitted contribution is the source-specific diagnosis of the September 2026 triad-triplet preprint: it identifies an omitted cross-triplet triad in the paper's own parameter example, evaluates its nonzero helical forcing, and thereby corrects the advertised exact-full-PDE interpretation while preserving the reduced ODE solution. Targeted searches found no prior public correction of this specific preprint.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The correction changes the mathematical status of the paper's central isolated-triplet object from an exact nonlinear Euler solution to an exact finite triad-network truncation. That distinction matters directly for the claimed benchmark and physical interpretation, and the explicit missing interaction makes the diagnosis reproducible rather than relying only on a general impossibility theorem.
